memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Every creature that moves along the ground is to be regarded as unclean; it is not to be eaten. You are not to eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it moves on its belly or walks on all fours or on many feet; it is unclean." - Lev 11:41-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that second verse again and notice how thoroughly God closes the door. On its belly. On all fours. On many feet. Every possible way a creature might move is covered. There is no clever exception left.

God knows us well. He knows the human instinct to find the gap — to obey the letter while hunting for the technicality. Jesus met this constantly among the religious leaders of His day, who could tithe their garden herbs with precision while neglecting justice, mercy and faithfulness (Matt 23:23).

We do it too, in quieter ways. We define honesty narrowly enough that our version of a story still counts as true. We keep the rule at work while breaking its whole purpose. We tell ourselves we have not technically done anything wrong.

But God is not after technical compliance. He is after our hearts. That is why He wrote laws that leave no loopholes — not to trap His people, but to train them, so that obedience would become a matter of love rather than legal minimum.

Under the New Covenant, God has gone further still. He writes His law on our hearts (Heb 8:10). Not a fence around us, but a new desire within us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have you been looking for a loophole rather than obeying God's heart?
2. Is your obedience driven by minimum requirement or by love?
3. What would change if you asked "what pleases God?" instead of "what am I allowed?"

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have obeyed the letter while missing Your heart. Write Your law within me, and make obedience a matter of love rather than loophole. Amen.
